name: Skill Tuner
tagline: Define what a good output looks like, score a real run against it, and get the one edit to make first — with a log so tuning compounds.
who: Anyone whose taught skill isn't producing what they want — or who wants to know if it's good enough to share.
how: Point the agent at a learned skill and one real run — a task it actually did. Together you pin down what good looks like as roughly three anchored 1–10 criteria; the agent scores the run with evidence for every number, then delivers three distinct paths to a 10 led by the one concrete edit to try first, with exact replacement text ready to apply. It applies the edit to the skill's file on its own computer, you re-run, it re-scores on the same scale, and a tuning log keeps failed experiments failed. Guardrails stop the scale from becoming a cage: it judges outputs, never procedure, and says so when the right fix isn't obvious.
